limitations: Readable secondary reporting substitutes for inaccessible primary disclosures and original reporting.

The schema permits only one contract metric_scope despite the two financial metrics.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Amazon, which spent $54 billion in capex last quarter, is taking about $3 billion of GPU deliveries every month 'for the foreseeable future' despite a supply glut that means it cannot install them, and in some cases it has no idea when it may do so.

statement.excerpt: That’s right folks — Amazon, which spent $54 billion in capex last quarter — is taking $3 billion worth of GPU deliveries every month “for the foreseeable future,” despite having such a supply glut that it cannot install them, and in some cases lacks an idea of when it may do so.

from_speaker: $3 billion worth of GPU deliveries every month
in some cases lacks an idea of when
our_interpretation: Read 'last quarter' as the latest reported quarter before publication: April–June 2026.
Read the delivery assertion as actual receipts under an ongoing procurement schedule. The surrounding quotation describes a projection, so actual receipts and planned receipts must be distinguished.
Read 'GPUs' as GPU-containing racks, consistent with the quoted reporting, rather than the value of bare GPU chips.
Read 'supply glut' as equipment exceeding immediate installation capacity at some Amazon sites, not proof of an industry-wide surplus.

The target period encompasses the separate quarterly spending assertion and the August–October procurement account. The contract's single metric_scope describes the principal delivery claim; capex is checked separately.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish approximately $54 billion of capex in the latest reported quarter, approximately $3 billion of actual monthly rack receipts after August, and some received equipment awaiting installation without a clear installation schedule.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially disprove the spending figure, recurring delivery amount, or reported installation backlog. A projection without confirmation is insufficient support, but is not itself a contradiction.
